          - Gap: no sufficiently specific source note found yet.
        - `062.03.04.02.09` Explain that Mode S transponders receive interrogations from TCAS and SSR ground stations. [TK M2; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: Interrogator/transmponder backwards compaticble, i.e., ground station can interrogate a mode A ac and mode S ac will still provide mode A and C response to old-style interrogations.
          - Aide-memoire: mode S transponders store and are able to transmit on request hundreds of aircraft parameters and have datalink capability (ground initiated comm B (GICB)).
          - Aide-memoire: mode S capable of up- and downlink; required for TCAS I or II.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Secondary Surveillance Radar SSR > SSR Mode S (match 1.16)
        - `062.03.04.02.10` State that Mode S interrogation contains either the aircraft address, selective call or all-call address. [TK M2; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: any mode A/C transponder receiving the all-call witll reply to the interrogation as normal, not recognising the P4 pulse.
          - Aide-memoire: ac will switch to mode S, if it receives P4 with its aircraft address and call sign.
          - Aide-memoire: mode S all call interogation starts of looking like Mode A or C interogation, but has a thrid extra pulse P4 after P3.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Secondary Surveillance Radar SSR > Mode A/C/S All Call (match 1.24)
        - `062.03.04.02.11` State that every aircraft is allocated an ICAO aircraft address, which is hard-coded into the Mode S transponder (Mode S address). [TK M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Validation note: _Validation needed against ICAO Annex 10 Vol IV Mode S specifications._
          - Aide-memoire: _Validation draft:_ Each Mode S-equipped aircraft uses a unique ICAO 24-bit aircraft address assigned by the responsible authority/state.
          - Aide-memoire: _Validation draft:_ The address is part of the Mode S/ADS-B identity data set and is normally configured in the aircraft equipment.
          - Source note: `validation supplement` > EASA CS-ACNS / ADS-B and Mode S surveillance material | Validation needed against ICAO Annex 10 Vol IV Mode S specifications. (match 9.99)
      - **`062.03.04.03` Presentation and interpretation**
        - `062.03.04.03.01` State that an aircraft can be identified by a unique code. [Exam M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Gap: no sufficiently specific source note found yet.
        - `062.03.04.03.02` State which information can be presented on the ATC display system: pressure altitude; flight level; flight number or aircraft registration number; GS. [Exam M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: Modern ATC radars tend to use computer generated displays (synthetic displays) rather than 'raw radar data'.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Radar Theory > ATC Radar Displays (match 1.04)
        - `062.03.04.03.03` Explain the use and function of the selector modes: OFF, Standby, ON (Mode A), ALT (Mode A, C and S), TEST, and of the reply lamp. [TK M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: selector: OFF, SBY, ON, ALT, TEST
          - Aide-memoire: ALT - power on system replies to mode A interrogation with selected code and mode C (altitude readout)
          - Aide-memoire: ON - power on, system replies to mode A with selected code
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Secondary Surveillance Radar SSR > Cockpit Equipment (match 0.76)
  - **`062.06.00.00` GLOBAL NAVIGATION SATELLITE SYSTEMS (GNSSs)**
    - **`062.06.01.00` Global navigation satellite systems (GNSSs)**
      - **`062.06.01.01` General**
        - `062.06.01.01.01` State that there are four main GNSSs. These are: USA NAVigation System with Timing And Ranging Global Positioning System (NAVSTAR GPS); Russian GLObal NAvigation Satellite System (GLONASS); European Galileo (under construction); Chinese BeiDou (under construction). [Exam M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: Navstar Global Poisioning System (GPS) ~ US DoD
          - Aide-memoire: GNSS Global Navigation Satellite System := "accurate" & world wide navigation system.
          - Aide-memoire: Global Orbiting Navigation Satellite System (GLOSNASS) ~ Commonwealth of Independent States (ex Soviet Union)
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Satellite Navigation (match 1.14)
        - `062.06.01.01.02` State that all four systems (will) consist of a constellation of satellites which can be used by a suitably equipped receiver to determine position. [TK M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: Continuous sampling allows faulty satellites to be identified and removed from the position calculation.
          - Aide-memoire: At a repeating time interval data from one of the four satellites is replaced by data from the spare/additional satellite.
          - Aide-memoire: satellites monitored from ground => delay before realising malfunction.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Satellite Augmentation Systems > ABAS (match 0.73)
      - **`062.06.01.02` Operation**
        - `062.06.01.02.01` State that there are currently two modes of operation: standard positioning service (SPS) for civilian users, and precise positioning service (PPS) for authorised users. [Exam M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: system for civilian use is called standard positioning service (SPS) and designed to provide users with a deliberately less accurate positioing service than for military.
          - Aide-memoire: military system uses both frequencies ~ "precise" possitioning service (PPS) and transmits a code called precise (P) or PY code.
          - Aide-memoire: GPS originally designed for US military = two frequencies in UHF.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Satellite Navigation > Frequencies (match 1.03)
        - `062.06.01.02.02` SPS was originally designed to provide civilian users with a less accurate positioning capability than PPS. [Exam M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: system for civilian use is called standard positioning service (SPS) and designed to provide users with a deliberately less accurate positioing service than for military.
          - Aide-memoire: GPS originally designed for US military = two frequencies in UHF.
          - Aide-memoire: US convention 'bands' (than clusters of frequencies) => "L"-band, 1575.42 MHz (L1) and 1227.6MHz (L2).
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Satellite Navigation > Frequencies (match 1.34)
        - `062.06.01.02.03` Name the three GNSS segments as follows: space segment; control segment; user segment. [TK M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: - space segment ~ constellation of satellites;
          - Aide-memoire: - user segment ~ receivers (typically on board of aircraft).
          - Aide-memoire: space segment ~ notional constellation := design minimum to make (GNS)system work.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Satellite Navigation > GNSS segments (match 1.70)
        - `062.06.01.02.09` State that an ionospheric model is used to calculate the time delay of the signal travelling through the ionosphere. [TK M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: **ionospheric model** ~ mathematical model of Ionoshere to allow compensating for single largest error of GPS with is the dealy to the signal as it passes through the ionosphere, based on 11 year solar cycle.
          - Aide-memoire: **satellite clock correction** ~ correction needed tfor timing signal from the transmitting satellite
          - Aide-memoire: **UTC correction** ~ determines difference between GPS time and UTC; UTC has leap seconds applied from time to time - GPS does not! Delta currently 18 seconds.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Satellite Navigation > NAV Message (match 0.77)
        - `062.06.01.02.11` State that satellites are equipped with atomic clocks which allow the system to keep very accurate time reference. [TK M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Gap: no sufficiently specific source note found yet.
        - `062.06.01.02.12` State that the control segment comprises: a master control station; a ground antenna; monitoring stations. [TK M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: - control segment ~ master control station, ground antennas, and monitor stations, compute corrections of orbital parameters, and up/download data;
          - Aide-memoire: - space segment ~ constellation of satellites;
          - Aide-memoire: - user segment ~ receivers (typically on board of aircraft).
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Satellite Navigation > GNSS segments (match 0.82)
        - `062.06.01.02.14` State that GNSS supplies three-dimensional position fixes and speed data, plus a precise time reference. [TK M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: Once satellites are identified, the position is computed from the more accurate ephemeris data.
          - Aide-memoire: purpose of Almanac = when receiver is first turned on, it looks for satellites where it expects to find them according to the almanac,and based on the time and its last known position.
          - Aide-memoire: Time to first fix can be shortened by entering a position, time, and date to give the receiver a new starting datum and shorten the search for the satellites.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Satellite Navigation > Time to First Fix (match 0.84)
        - `062.06.01.02.15` State that a GNSS receiver is able to determine the distance to a satellite by determining the difference between the time of transmission by the satellite and the time of reception. [TK M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: purpose of Almanac = when receiver is first turned on, it looks for satellites where it expects to find them according to the almanac,and based on the time and its last known position.
          - Aide-memoire: Time to first fix can be shortened by entering a position, time, and date to give the receiver a new starting datum and shorten the search for the satellites.
          - Aide-memoire: If receiver has been moved a long way simnce it was last used, it gets confused and has to search the sky to determine which satellites are overhead: This can take up to 4 or 5 minutes.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Satellite Navigation > Time to First Fix (match 0.84)
        - `062.06.01.02.16` State that the initial distance calculated to the satellites is called pseudo-range because the difference between the GNSS receiver and the satellite time references initially creates an erroneous range. [TK M2; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: Thus, due to receiver clock inaccuracy, the initial calculated range from the satellite is invariably inaccurate := pseudo range.
          - Aide-memoire: Correction for receiver clock bias ensures that by the time a fix position is calculated, the receiver is completely synchronised to satellite time.
          - Aide-memoire: Pseude ranges from several satellites calculated by a receiver with clock bias would produce a poorly defined fix.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Satellite Navigation > Pseudo Ranges (match 1.12)
        - `062.06.01.02.17` State that each range defines a sphere with its centre at the satellite. [TK M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Gap: no sufficiently specific source note found yet.
        - `062.06.01.02.18` State that there are four unknown parameters (x, y, z and Delta t) (receiver clock error) which require the measurement of ranges to four different satellites in order to get the position. [TK M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: Continuous sampling allows faulty satellites to be identified and removed from the position calculation.
          - Aide-memoire: At a repeating time interval data from one of the four satellites is replaced by data from the spare/additional satellite.
          - Aide-memoire: If the calculated position changes => either satellite was taken out of the fixing calculation or the new one was brought in is in error.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Satellite Augmentation Systems > ABAS (match 0.71)
        - `062.06.01.02.19` State that the GNSS receiver is able to synchronise to the correct time reference when receiving four satellites. [TK M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: purpose of Almanac = when receiver is first turned on, it looks for satellites where it expects to find them according to the almanac,and based on the time and its last known position.
          - Aide-memoire: Time to first fix can be shortened by entering a position, time, and date to give the receiver a new starting datum and shorten the search for the satellites.
          - Aide-memoire: If receiver has been moved a long way simnce it was last used, it gets confused and has to search the sky to determine which satellites are overhead: This can take up to 4 or 5 minutes.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Satellite Navigation > Time to First Fix (match 0.93)
        - `062.06.01.02.20` State that the receiver is able to calculate aircraft ground speed using the space vehicle (SV) Doppler frequency shift or the change in receiver position over time. [TK M2; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: low end GPS reeivers comute velocity from the change in receiver position over time ~ accuracy in order of meters a second.
          - Aide-memoire: Sophisticated receivers use Doppler shift on the received signal, compute out the satellite velocity in 3 dimensions and are left with the receiver velocity to accuracy of centimeters a second.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Satellite Navigation > Velocity (match 1.06)
        - `062.06.01.02.21` Define 'receiver autonomous integrity monitoring (RAIM)' as a technique that ensures the integrity of the provided data by redundant measurements. [Exam M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: receiver autonomous integrity monitoring (RAIM) -> basic RAIM uses one additional satellite above the 4 required ones for a 3D fix, i.e., 5.
          - Aide-memoire: RAIM operation may be described as 'using redundant range measurement to support FD and FDE operation'.
          - Aide-memoire: To continue integrity monitoring function, there must be an additional spare satellite, Fault Detection and Exclusion (FDE).
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Satellite Augmentation Systems > ABAS (match 0.85)
        - `062.06.01.02.22` State that RAIM is achieved by consistency checks among range measurements. [Exam M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Gap: no sufficiently specific source note found yet.
    - **`062.06.02.00` Ground-, satellite- and aircraft-based augmentation systems**
      - **`062.06.02.02` Satellite-based augmentation systems (SBASs)**
        - `062.06.02.02.01` Explain the principle of an SBAS: to measure on the ground the errors in the signals received from the satellites and transmit differential corrections and integrity messages for navigation satellites. [TK M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: SBAS apply principle over a wide(r) area using satellites to transmit correction data to aircraft.
          - Aide-memoire: SBAS uses same architecture as GPS: 3 segments: ground segment, space segment, and a user segment consisting of airborne SBAS receivers.
          - Aide-memoire: SBAS improves integrity and safety. EGNOS alerts users within 6 seconds, if a GPS malfunction occurs; which EASA compare to up to 3hrs using GPS alone.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Satellite Augmentation Systems > Satellite Based Augmentation Systems SBAS (match 1.14)
        - `062.06.02.02.02` State that the frequency band of the data link is identical to that of the GPS signals. [TK M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Gap: no sufficiently specific source note found yet.
        - `062.06.02.02.03` Explain that the use of geostationary satellites enables messages to be broadcast over very wide areas. [TK M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Gap: no sufficiently specific source note found yet.
        - `062.06.02.02.04` State that pseudo-range measurements to these geostationary satellites can also be made, as if they were GPS satellites. [TK M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Gap: no sufficiently specific source note found yet.
        - `062.06.02.02.05` State that SBAS consists of two elements: ground infrastructure (monitoring and processing stations); communication satellites. [TK M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: SBAS does not need to be located within 20NM of a reference stations.
          - Aide-memoire: SBAS apply principle over a wide(r) area using satellites to transmit correction data to aircraft.
          - Aide-memoire: SBAS uses same architecture as GPS: 3 segments: ground segment, space segment, and a user segment consisting of airborne SBAS receivers.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Satellite Augmentation Systems > Satellite Based Augmentation Systems SBAS (match 0.95)
        - `062.06.02.02.06` State that SBAS allows the implementation of three-dimensional Type A and Type B approaches. [Exam M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: SBAS allow for the implementation of 3D Type A and Type B approaches ~ approach procedure with vertical guidance APV.
          - Aide-memoire: Example of SBAS approach plate.
          - Aide-memoire: A,B old ICAO Annex 6 classification ~ type A := decision height of not less than 250ft, type B DH not less than 200ft.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Satellite Augmentation Systems > SBAS Approaches (match 1.47)
        - `062.06.02.02.07` State the following examples of SBAS: European Geostationary Navigation Overlay Service (EGNOS) in western Europe and the Mediterranean; wide area augmentation system (WAAS) in the USA; multi-functional transport satellite (MTSAT)-based augmentation system (MSAS) in Japan; GPS and geostationary earth orbit augmented navigation (GAGAN) in India. [TK M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: + EGNOS - European Geostationary Navigation Overlay System, Western Europe and Mediterranean.
          - Aide-memoire: + MSAS - multi-functional satellite augmentation system, Japan
          - Aide-memoire: SBAS space segment := geostationary satellite system ~ allows for transmission of the message over a wide area.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Satellite Augmentation Systems > Satellite Based Augmentation Systems SBAS (match 1.80)
        - `062.06.02.02.08` State that SBAS is designed to significantly improve accuracy and integrity. [TK M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: satellite based augmentation systems (SBAS) ~ integrity data is relayed through a satellite link.
          - Aide-memoire: GBAS and SBAS provide also a theoretical increase in fixing accuracy, differential GPS.
          - Aide-memoire: airborne based augmentation systems (ABAS) ~ receiver or other aircraft systems provide integrity monitoring
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Satellite Augmentation Systems (match 1.24)
        - `062.06.02.02.09` Explain that integrity and safety are improved by alerting SBAS users within 6 seconds if a GPS malfunction occurs. [Exam M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: SBAS improves integrity and safety. EGNOS alerts users within 6 seconds, if a GPS malfunction occurs; which EASA compare to up to 3hrs using GPS alone.
          - Aide-memoire: SBAS does not need to be located within 20NM of a reference stations.
          - Aide-memoire: SBAS uses same architecture as GPS: 3 segments: ground segment, space segment, and a user segment consisting of airborne SBAS receivers.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Satellite Augmentation Systems > Satellite Based Augmentation Systems SBAS (match 1.19)
      - **`062.06.02.04` Aircraft-based augmentation systems (ABASs)**
        - `062.06.02.04.01` Explain the principle of ABAS: to use redundant elements within the GPS constellation (e.g. multiplicity of distance measurements to various satellites) or the combination of GNSS measurements with those of other navigation sensors (such as inertial systems) in order to develop integrity control. [Exam M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: improve integrity within the ac by combining positioning with more conventional navigation systems to create a multi-sensor navigation system, including use of other inputs such as barometric altitude and time.
          - Aide-memoire: The input from other systems can identify when the GPS position is in error := aircraft autonomous integrity monitoring AAIM.
          - Aide-memoire: Note: neither component of ABAS, neither RAIM nor AAIM, improves satellite navigation accuracy.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Satellite Augmentation Systems > ABAS > Note - Exam (match 0.93)
        - `062.06.02.04.02` State that the type of ABAS using only GNSS information is named receiver autonomous integrity monitoring (RAIM). [Exam M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: Note: neither component of ABAS, neither RAIM nor AAIM, improves satellite navigation accuracy.
          - Aide-memoire: Aircraft Autonomous Integrity Monitoring (AAIM)
          - Aide-memoire: They only provide INTEGRITY MONITORING!
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Satellite Augmentation Systems > ABAS > Note - Exam (match 0.98)
        - `062.06.02.04.03` State that a system using information from additional onboard sensors is named aircraft autonomous integrity monitoring (AAIM). [Exam M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Validation note: _Validation needed against ICAO Doc 9613._
          - Aide-memoire: _Validation draft:_ AAIM means aircraft autonomous integrity monitoring.
          - Aide-memoire: _Validation draft:_ Unlike basic RAIM, AAIM may use additional onboard sensors beyond GNSS to support integrity monitoring.
          - Source note: `validation supplement` > EASA Air Ops PBN material; ICAO Doc 9613 integrity-monitoring topic | Validation needed against ICAO Doc 9613. (match 9.99)
        - `062.06.02.04.04` Explain that the typical sensors used are barometric altimeter and inertial reference system (IRS). [Exam M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Validation note: _Validation needed against ICAO Annex 10, Doc 9613 and Doc 9849._
          - Aide-memoire: _Validation draft:_ Typical supplemental sensors feeding navigation/monitoring include barometric altitude and inertial reference data.
          - Aide-memoire: _Validation draft:_ GNSS/FMS integrity or position calculations may use inertial/barometric inputs depending on architecture and certification basis.
          - Source note: `validation supplement` > EASA CS-ACNS and Air Ops PBN material; ICAO Doc 9613/9849 references | Validation needed against ICAO Annex 10, Doc 9613 and Doc 9849. (match 9.99)
  - **`062.07.00.00` PERFORMANCE-BASED NAVIGATION (PBN)**
    - **`062.07.01.00` Performance-based navigation (PBN) concept (as described in ICAO Doc 9613)**
      - **`062.07.01.01` PBN principles**
        - `062.07.01.01.01` List the factors used to define area navigation (RNAV) or required navigation performance (RNP) system performance requirements (accuracy, integrity and continuity). [TK M3; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: + **continuity** ~ capability of the system to perform its function without unscheduled interruptions during the intended operation.
          - Aide-memoire: + **integrity** ~ measure of trust in the correctness of the information supplied by the whole system. Integrity includes the ability of the system to provide timely and valid alerts to the user.
          - Aide-memoire: + **accuracy** ~ difference between true and indicated position ~ "conformance" of true position with the required position
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Performance Based Navigation (PBN) Concepts > RNAV or RNP System Performance Requirements (match 2.17)
        - `062.07.01.01.02` State that these RNAV and RNP systems are necessary to optimise the utilisation of available airspace. [TK M2/M3; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: no requirement for dual RNAV systems => alternative means of navigation myst be available -> ground based NAVAID infrastructure is essential in RNAV5 airspace, although gaps in coverage are permitted.
          - Aide-memoire: RNAV 5 allows operation in enroute continental areas by ac with surprisingly basic navigation equipment.
          - Aide-memoire: AC must have an RNAV system using one or more VOR/DME, DME/DME, INS or IRS, or GNSS.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Specific RNAV and RNP Specification > RNAV5 (match 1.54)
        - `062.07.01.01.03` State that it is necessary for flight crew and air traffic controllers to be aware of the on-board RNAV or RNP system capabilities in order to determine whether the performance of the RNAV or RNP system is appropriate for the specific airspace requirements. [TK M2/M3; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: pilots and ATCOs must be aware of the on-board RNAV or RNP system capabilities in order to determine whether the performance of the system is appropriate for the airspace requirements.
          - Aide-memoire: EASA only requires specific approval of some PBN procedures, e.g. RNP AR APCH and RNP0.3.
          - Aide-memoire: => pilots must have RNP endoresement on their instrument rating
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > PBN Operations > Approval of Operator, Equipment, and Procedures (match 1.62)
        - `062.07.01.01.04` Define accuracy as the conformance of the true position and the required position. [TK M2/M3; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: + **accuracy** ~ difference between true and indicated position ~ "conformance" of true position with the required position
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Performance Based Navigation (PBN) Concepts > RNAV or RNP System Performance Requirements (match 0.91)
        - `062.07.01.01.05` Define continuity as the capability of the system to perform its function without unscheduled interruptions during the intended operation. [Exam M2; TK M3; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: + **continuity** ~ capability of the system to perform its function without unscheduled interruptions during the intended operation.
          - Aide-memoire: + **integrity** ~ measure of trust in the correctness of the information supplied by the whole system. Integrity includes the ability of the system to provide timely and valid alerts to the user.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Performance Based Navigation (PBN) Concepts > RNAV or RNP System Performance Requirements (match 1.68)
        - `062.07.01.01.06` Define integrity as a measure of the trust that can be placed in the correctness of the information supplied by the total system. Integrity includes the ability of a system to provide timely and valid alerts to the user. [Exam M2; TK M3; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: + **integrity** ~ measure of trust in the correctness of the information supplied by the whole system. Integrity includes the ability of the system to provide timely and valid alerts to the user.
          - Aide-memoire: + **continuity** ~ capability of the system to perform its function without unscheduled interruptions during the intended operation.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Performance Based Navigation (PBN) Concepts > RNAV or RNP System Performance Requirements (match 1.91)
        - `062.07.01.01.07` State that, unlike conventional navigation, PBN is not sensor-specific. [Exam M2; TK M3; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: there exists some PBN functionality requirements and some specific requirements for certain levels of RNAV and RNP.
          - Aide-memoire: sometimes referred to as 4th PBN system requirement.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Performance Based Navigation (PBN) Concepts > Functionality (match 1.42)
        - `062.07.01.01.08` Explain the difference between raw data and computed data. [Exam M2; TK M3; CBIR; IR]
          - Validation note: _Validation needed against ICAO Doc 9613._
          - Aide-memoire: _Validation draft:_ Raw data is direct navigation-sensor information, e.g. VOR/LOC/ADF/DME indications.
          - Aide-memoire: _Validation draft:_ Computed data is processed by an RNAV/FMS system, e.g. calculated position, track, distance, ETA or guidance derived from several inputs/database data.

    - **`062.07.02.00` Navigation specifications**
      - **`062.07.02.01` Area navigation (RNAV) and required navigation performance (RNP)**
        - `062.07.02.01.01` State the difference between RNAV and RNP in terms of the requirement for on-board performance monitoring and alerting. [Exam M2; TK M3; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: RNPeeb, RNAV does not required on-board performance monitoring and alerting system. Apart from this, accuracy requirements between RNAV2, RNAV1, RNP1, and RNP2 are basically THE SAME.
          - Aide-memoire: aircrew to use SID or STAR under these navigation specifications, if they can retrieve it from an on-board navigation database by name and verify it as matching the charted route.
          - Aide-memoire: Route can be modified through the insertion (from the database) or deletion of specific waypoints, in response to ATCO clearances.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Specific RNAV and RNP Specification > RNAV1, RNAV2, RNP1, RNP2 (match 1.68)
      - **`062.07.02.03` Designation of RNP and RNAV specifications**
        - `062.07.02.03.01` Interpret X in RNAV X or RNP X as the lateral navigation (LNAV) accuracy (total system error) in nautical miles, which is expected to be achieved at least 95 per cent of the flight time by the population of aircraft operating within the given airspace, route or procedure. [Exam M2; TK M3; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: Expected to be achieved 95% of the time by the population of ac operating within the airspace, route, or procedure.
          - Aide-memoire: PBN airspace navigation standards specified as RNP X or RNAV X.
          - Aide-memoire: X designates the lateral and longitudinal navigation accuracy in Nautical Miles.

          - Aide-memoire: to meet RNAV4 (X = 4) navigation specification, the Total System Error must be less than 4NM (X NM) for 95% of the time.

        - `062.07.02.03.09` State that required navigation performance approach (RNP APCH) is used in the approach phase of flight. [Exam M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: Thus, vertical guidance is not part of the approach.
          - Aide-memoire: LNAV approaches are constructed in the FMS when pilot slects the approach from a database by name.
          - Aide-memoire: It then constructs a lateral path using the path terminators specified for the approach, and displays the approach procedure for the pilots.

        - `062.07.02.03.10` State that required navigation performance authorisation required approach (RNP AR APCH) is used in the approach phase of flight. [Exam M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: Thus, vertical guidance is not part of the approach.
          - Aide-memoire: LNAV approaches are constructed in the FMS when pilot slects the approach from a database by name.

    - **`062.07.03.00` Use of performance-based navigation (PBN)**
      - **`062.07.03.03` Specific RNAV and RNP system functions**
        - `062.07.03.03.01` Recognise the definition of radius to fix (RF) leg. [Exam M2; TK M3; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: RADIUS-TO-FIX LEG (RF leg) ~ requirement for a specific curved path in a terminal or approach procedures (low-level procedure); defined as a radius, an arc length, and the fix at which it ends.
          - Aide-memoire: Example: RF-leg starts at waypoint EA123 and ends at waypoint EA125. Procedure defined as radius and arc distance; formally, start point not part of the "definition" (arc starts passing this point).
          - Aide-memoire: FIXED RADIUS TRANSITION ~ transition from route leg to another leg/segment other than simple fly-by waypoint; used in en-route airspace.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Performance Based Navigation (PBN) Concepts > Specific Requirements (match 0.72)
        - `062.07.03.03.02` Recognise the definition of a fixed radius transition (FRT). [Exam M2; TK M3; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: FIXED RADIUS TRANSITION ~ transition from route leg to another leg/segment other than simple fly-by waypoint; used in en-route airspace.
          - Aide-memoire: transition with a specified radius.
          - Aide-memoire: Example: RF-leg starts at waypoint EA123 and ends at waypoint EA125. Procedure defined as radius and arc distance; formally, start point not part of the "definition" (arc starts passing this point).
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Performance Based Navigation (PBN) Concepts > Specific Requirements (match 0.81)
        - `062.07.03.03.03` State the importance of respecting the flight director guidance and the speed constraints associated with an RF procedure. [Exam M2; TK M3; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: NOTE: important to follow flight director guidance and the speed constraints associated with an RF procedures.
          - Aide-memoire: If not, the correct path (and obstacle clearance) over ground will not be followed.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Performance Based Navigation (PBN) Concepts > Specific Requirements (match 0.78)
        - `062.07.03.03.04` Explain the difference between a fly-by-turn and a fly-over. [Exam M2; TK M3; CBIR; IR]
          - Validation note: _Validation needed against ICAO Doc 9613 and Doc 8168._
          - Aide-memoire: _Validation draft:_ A fly-by waypoint permits turn anticipation so the aircraft rolls into the next leg before crossing the waypoint.
          - Aide-memoire: _Validation draft:_ A fly-over waypoint must be crossed before the turn to the next leg is initiated.
          - Source note: `validation supplement` > EASA Air Ops PBN material and FAA AIM PBN waypoint explanation | Validation needed against ICAO Doc 9613 and Doc 8168. (match 9.99)
        - `062.07.03.03.07` Define the term 'offset flight path'. [Exam M2; TK M3; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: "Strategic Lateral Offset Procedures SLOP"
          - Aide-memoire: modern ac have capability to offset track in 0.1NM increments := micro SLOP.
          - Aide-memoire: Offsets continue past waypoints, paralleling each leg at the specified distance from the defined path/track.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Performance Based Navigation (PBN) Concepts > GENERAL REQUIREMENTS > Offset Flight Paths (match 1.20)
    - **`062.07.04.00` Performance-based navigation (PBN) operations**
      - **`062.07.04.01` Performance-based navigation (PBN) principles**
        - `062.07.04.01.01` Define 'path definition error' (PDE). [Exam M2; TK M3; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: path definition error PDE - inability of the system to accurately specify the desired path
          - Aide-memoire: flight technical error FTE - error relating to execution of flight along a defined path.
          - Aide-memoire: TSE = PDE + FTE + NSE.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Performance Based Navigation (PBN) Concepts > Accuracy (match 0.83)
        - `062.07.04.01.02` Define 'flight technical error' (FTE) and state that the FTE is the error in following the prescribed path, either by the auto-flight system or by the pilot. [Exam M2; TK M3; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: flight technical error FTE - error relating to execution of flight along a defined path.
          - Aide-memoire: path definition error PDE - inability of the system to accurately specify the desired path
          - Aide-memoire: PBN navigation specification refer to total system error TSE.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Performance Based Navigation (PBN) Concepts > Accuracy (match 0.73)
        - `062.07.04.01.03` Define 'navigation system error' (NSE) and state that the accuracy of a navigation system may be referred to as NSE. [Exam M2; TK M3; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: navigation system error NSE - inability to dermine actual position (e.g. sensor failure) or the limits of accuracy of GNSS, IRS, or DME.
          - Aide-memoire: PBN navigation specification refer to total system error TSE.
          - Aide-memoire: path definition error PDE - inability of the system to accurately specify the desired path
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Performance Based Navigation (PBN) Concepts > Accuracy (match 1.24)
        - `062.07.04.01.04` Define 'total system error' (TSE) and state that the geometric sum of the PDE, FTE and NSE equals the TSE. [Exam M2; TK M3; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: TSE = PDE + FTE + NSE.
          - Aide-memoire: PBN navigation specification refer to total system error TSE.
          - Aide-memoire: path definition error PDE - inability of the system to accurately specify the desired path
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Performance Based Navigation (PBN) Concepts > Accuracy (match 0.90)
      - **`062.07.04.02` On-board performance monitoring and alerting**
        - `062.07.04.02.01` State that on-board performance monitoring and alerting of flight technical errors is managed by on-board systems or flight crew procedures. [Exam M2; TK M3; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: RNP operations require on-board performance monitoring and alerting systems (PNbeeP).
          - Aide-memoire: If navigation capability is degraded for any reason, resulting in PBN capability not being maintained, the flight crew must inform ATC.
          - Aide-memoire: This can be as simple as radar monitoring by ATC, or it may involve changes of flight level and/or routing.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > PBN Operations > Estimated Position Error (match 1.00)
        - `062.07.04.02.02` State that on-board performance monitoring and alerting of navigation system errors is a requirement of on-board equipment for RNP. [Exam M2; TK M3; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: RNP specifications include a requirement for on-board performance monitoring and alerting.
          - Aide-memoire: RNAV specifications do not include any requirement of on-board monitoring and alerting.
          - Aide-memoire: PBN airspace navigation standards specified as RNP X or RNAV X.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Performance Based Navigation (PBN) Concepts > Navigation Specifications (match 1.44)
        - `062.07.04.02.06` State that on-board performance monitoring and alerting of path definition error is managed by gross reasonableness checks of navigation data. [Exam M2; TK M3; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: excessive path definition error PDE prevented by checks on navigation data, including checks on total flight plan distance for a flight with short distances between waypoints.
          - Aide-memoire: Flight Technical Error FTE is pilot or autopilot error in following the route indicated by the FMC. Can be managed by onboard systems.
          - Aide-memoire: crew procedures ~ cross-checks and/or mandatory use of autopilot in some airspaces.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > PBN Operations > Controlling TSE (match 1.11)
      - **`062.07.04.03` Abnormal situations**
        - `062.07.04.03.01` State that abnormal and contingency procedures are to be used in case of loss of the PBN capability. [Exam M2; TK M3; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: If navigation capability is degraded for any reason, resulting in PBN capability not being maintained, the flight crew must inform ATC.
          - Aide-memoire: ABNORMAL and CONTINGENCY procedures set for the airspace in quiestion are to then to be followed.
          - Aide-memoire: RNP operations require on-board performance monitoring and alerting systems (PNbeeP).
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > PBN Operations > Estimated Position Error (match 1.49)
      - **`062.07.04.04` Database management**
        - `062.07.04.04.01` State that, unless otherwise specified in the operations documentation or acceptable means of compliance (AMCs), the navigational database must be valid for the current aeronautical information regulation and control (AIRAC) cycle. [Exam M2; TK M3; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: flight crew has to CHECK that aeronautical database(s) is/are VALID for the current AIRAC cycle during pre-flight preparation.
          - Aide-memoire: Navigation data is pulished under set of rules: AIRAC Aeronautical Information Regulation and Control.
          - Aide-memoire: ==> accuracy, resolution, and integrity must be safeguarded.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > PBN Operations > CHECKING AIRAC CYCLE (match 1.04)
    - **`062.07.05.00` Requirements of specific RNAV and RNP specifications**
      - **`062.07.05.02` RNAV 5**
        - `062.07.05.02.01` State that manual data entry is acceptable for RNAV 5. [Exam M2; TK M3; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: navigation database NOT required under RNAV5 => manual entry of data such as waypoints is permitted.
          - Aide-memoire: RNAV 5 allows operation in enroute continental areas by ac with surprisingly basic navigation equipment.
          - Aide-memoire: AC must have an RNAV system using one or more VOR/DME, DME/DME, INS or IRS, or GNSS.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Specific RNAV and RNP Specification > RNAV5 (match 1.25)
      - **`062.07.05.03` RNAV 1/RNAV 2/RNP 1/RNP 2**
        - `062.07.05.03.01` State that pilots must not fly an RNAV 1, RNAV 2, RNP 1 or RNP 2 standard instrument departure (SID) or standard instrument arrival (STAR) unless it is retrievable by route name from the on-board navigation database and conforms to the charted route. [Exam M2; TK M3; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: aircrew to use SID or STAR under these navigation specifications, if they can retrieve it from an on-board navigation database by name and verify it as matching the charted route.
          - Aide-memoire: RNPeeb, RNAV does not required on-board performance monitoring and alerting system. Apart from this, accuracy requirements between RNAV2, RNAV1, RNP1, and RNP2 are basically THE SAME.
          - Aide-memoire: Route can be modified through the insertion (from the database) or deletion of specific waypoints, in response to ATCO clearances.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Specific RNAV and RNP Specification > RNAV1, RNAV2, RNP1, RNP2 (match 1.85)
        - `062.07.05.03.02` State that the route may subsequently be modified through the insertion (from the database) or deletion of specific waypoints in response to ATC clearances. [Exam M2; TK M3; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: Route can be modified through the insertion (from the database) or deletion of specific waypoints, in response to ATCO clearances.
          - Aide-memoire: Once activated, and in response to clearances from ATC, the aircrew may delete waypoints or insert new waypoints, but only waypoints already in the database.
          - Aide-memoire: However, manual entry or creation of new waypoints in the database by manual entry of latitude and longitude, or place/bearing/distance, is NOT PERMITTED.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Specific RNAV and RNP Specification > RNAV1, RNAV2, RNP1, RNP2 (match 1.62)
        - `062.07.05.03.03` State that the manual entry, or creation of new waypoints by manual entry, of either latitude and longitude or place/bearing/distance values is not permitted. [Exam M2; TK M3; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: However, manual entry or creation of new waypoints in the database by manual entry of latitude and longitude, or place/bearing/distance, is NOT PERMITTED.
          - Aide-memoire: Once activated, and in response to clearances from ATC, the aircrew may delete waypoints or insert new waypoints, but only waypoints already in the database.
          - Aide-memoire: Route can be modified through the insertion (from the database) or deletion of specific waypoints, in response to ATCO clearances.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Specific RNAV and RNP Specification > RNAV1, RNAV2, RNP1, RNP2 (match 1.28)
      - **`062.07.05.05` Required navigation performance approach (RNP APCH)**
        - `062.07.05.05.01` State that pilots must not fly an RNP APCH unless it is retrievable by procedure name from the on-board navigation database and conforms to the charted procedure. [Exam M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: RNP APCH may be lateral only LNAV, which is a non-precision approach, or lateral and vertical, which fall into the new category "approach with vertical guidance".
          - Aide-memoire: GNSS primary navigation system to support RNP APCH procedures, although missed approah procedures (e.g. checking altitude at a specified point on approach).
          - Aide-memoire: Pilots can only use an approach that can be retrieved by name form an on-board navigation database, and it is verified to match the charted route.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Specific RNAV and RNP Specification > RNP APCH (match 1.53)
        - `062.07.05.05.02` State that an RNP APCH to LNAV minima is a non-precision IAP designed for two-dimensional approach operations. [Exam M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: RNP APCH may be lateral only LNAV, which is a non-precision approach, or lateral and vertical, which fall into the new category "approach with vertical guidance".
          - Aide-memoire: GNSS primary navigation system to support RNP APCH procedures, although missed approah procedures (e.g. checking altitude at a specified point on approach).
          - Aide-memoire: Pilots can only use an approach that can be retrieved by name form an on-board navigation database, and it is verified to match the charted route.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Specific RNAV and RNP Specification > RNP APCH (match 1.42)
        - `062.07.05.05.03` State that an RNP APCH to lateral navigation (LNAV)/vertical navigation (VNAV) minima has lateral guidance based on GNSS and vertical guidance based on either SBAS or barometric vertical navigation (Baro-VNAV). [Exam M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: approach and landing operations with vertical guidance - lateral guidance is based on the required navigation procedures (RNP), approach (APCH) specifications and baro VNAV is required.
          - Aide-memoire: baro VNAV equipment is the Vertical Navigation element of an FMS with an additonal barometric altitude input into the FMS.
          - Aide-memoire: non-precision approaches - baro VNAV is not required but is used to assist the continuous descent final approach CDFA technique
          - Source note: `010-air-law.qmd` > Departure Procedures > Baro VNAV (match 1.62)
        - `062.07.05.05.04` State that an RNP APCH to LNAV/VNAV minima may only be conducted with vertical guidance certified for the purpose. [Exam M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: RNP APCH may be lateral only LNAV, which is a non-precision approach, or lateral and vertical, which fall into the new category "approach with vertical guidance".
          - Aide-memoire: GNSS primary navigation system to support RNP APCH procedures, although missed approah procedures (e.g. checking altitude at a specified point on approach).
          - Aide-memoire: Pilots can only use an approach that can be retrieved by name form an on-board navigation database, and it is verified to match the charted route.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Specific RNAV and RNP Specification > RNP APCH (match 1.42)
        - `062.07.05.05.05` Explain why an RNP APCH to LNAV/VNAV minima based on Baro-VNAV may only be conducted when the aerodrome temperature is within a promulgated range if the barometric input is not automatically temperature-compensated. [Exam M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: approach and landing operations with vertical guidance - lateral guidance is based on the required navigation procedures (RNP), approach (APCH) specifications and baro VNAV is required.
          - Aide-memoire: baro VNAV equipment is the Vertical Navigation element of an FMS with an additonal barometric altitude input into the FMS.
          - Aide-memoire: non-precision approaches - baro VNAV is not required but is used to assist the continuous descent final approach CDFA technique
          - Source note: `010-air-law.qmd` > Departure Procedures > Baro VNAV (match 1.38)
        - `062.07.05.05.06` State that the correct altimeter setting is critical for the safe conduct of an RNP APCH using Baro-VNAV. [Exam M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: guidance is based on barometric references, altimeter setting discipline is crucial to conduct safe VNAV approach.
          - Aide-memoire: Note: many operator use radio altimeter to crosscheck the barometric setting of the approach
          - Aide-memoire: some ac can correct for air temperature - NOT A REQUIREMENT for certification.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Specific RNAV and RNP Specification > RNP APCH - APV Approaches > Air Temperature Correction (match 1.52)
        - `062.07.05.05.07` State that an RNP APCH to LNAV/VNAV minima is a three-dimensional operation. [Exam M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: STRICTLY speaking, NO GLIDEPATH ==> MDA is used which will be higher than the Decision ALtitude DA or an LNAV/VNAV approach to the same runway.
          - Aide-memoire: LNAV approaches are constructed in the FMS when pilot slects the approach from a database by name.
          - Aide-memoire: FMS uses the end point (known as the "anchor" point) located on the extended runway centerline, and a suitable distance from the runway threshold for a landing to be made, based on the Minimum Descent Altitude MDA.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Specific RNAV and RNP Specification > RNP APCH LNAV Approach (match 1.44)
        - `062.07.05.05.08` State that an RNP APCH to localiser performance with vertical guidance (LPV) minima is a three-dimensional operation. [Exam M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: RNP approaches with vertical guidance := APV approach
          - Aide-memoire: Vertical guidance from any other source invalidates the use of VNAV minima.
          - Aide-memoire: APV Baro Approaches, vertical guidance VNAV and may include RNAV or RNAV GNSS to indicate lateral part of the approach.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Specific RNAV and RNP Specification > RNP APCH - APV Approaches (match 1.36)
        - `062.07.05.05.09` State that RNP APCH to LPV minima requires a final approach segment (FAS) data block. [Exam M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: This data is knows as the Final Approach Segment FAS data block.
          - Aide-memoire: In order to use LPV minima, the FAS data block must be used to create the approach.
          - Aide-memoire: APC approaches using SBAS can be also known as Localiser Performance with Vetical Guidance LPV approaches.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Specific RNAV and RNP Specification > APV SBAS Approaches (match 1.39)
        - `062.07.05.05.10` State that RNP approaches to LPV minima require SBAS. [Exam M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: APC approaches using SBAS can be also known as Localiser Performance with Vetical Guidance LPV approaches.
          - Aide-memoire: for approaches with great precision requirement, the small errors inherent in GNSS can be a problem.
          - Aide-memoire: In order to use LPV minima, the FAS data block must be used to create the approach.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Specific RNAV and RNP Specification > APV SBAS Approaches (match 1.82)
        - `062.07.05.05.11` State that the FAS data block is a standard data format to describe the final approach path. [Exam M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: FAP is a point in space on the centre line of the localiser or the MLS azimut specified for the final approach track where the intermediate approach alt/height intersects the nominal glide path or MLS elevation angle.
          - Aide-memoire: final approach segment begins at FAF - if there is one.
          - Aide-memoire: The FAF should not be more than 10NM from landing surface.
          - Source note: `010-air-law.qmd` > Approach Procedures > Final Approach Fix and Final Approach Point (match 0.71)
      - **`062.07.05.06` Required navigation performance authorisation required approach (RNP AR APCH)**
        - `062.07.05.06.01` State that RNP AR APCH requires authorisation. [Exam M2; CBIR; IR]
          - Aide-memoire: RNP APCH may be lateral only LNAV, which is a non-precision approach, or lateral and vertical, which fall into the new category "approach with vertical guidance".
          - Aide-memoire: GNSS primary navigation system to support RNP APCH procedures, although missed approah procedures (e.g. checking altitude at a specified point on approach).
          - Aide-memoire: Pilots can only use an approach that can be retrieved by name form an on-board navigation database, and it is verified to match the charted route.
          - Source note: `060-radio-navigation.qmd` > Specific RNAV and RNP Specification > RNP APCH (match 1.58)

## 090 Communications

          - Aide-memoire: Levels at holding points should be assigned so that -- normally the first ac to arrive over a holding point should be at the lowest level, with following ac at successively higher levels. <--> stack!
          - Aide-memoire: holding and holding pattern entry shall be accomplished in accordance with procedures established by the approiate ATS Authority and published in the relevant AIP.

          - Aide-memoire: No invitation to change from IFR to VFR shall be made by ATS either directly or by inference.
          - Aide-memoire: Change from IFR to VFR flight shall only acceptable when a message initiated by the pilot-in-command containing the specific expressing CANCELLING MY IFR FLIGHT together with the changes, if any, to be made to the current flight plan is received by an ATS...
          - Aide-memoire: ac operating under IFR encouters VMC shall not cancle its IFR flight unless it is anticipated and intended that the flight will be continued for a reasonable perriod of time in uniterrupted VMC.

          - Aide-memoire: routine met observations are made at ATS reporting points roughly an hour apart or when requested.
          - Aide-memoire: ac exemptd from making routine observations when the flight duration is 2 hours or less, when the aircraft is wihin one hour of landing and when it is below 1500m (5000ft).
          - Aide-memoire: observations during climb of meteorological conditions or approach phases of flight not previously reported to the pilot-in-command which in his opinion are likely to affect the safety of other ac operations must be reporting in the AIREP format.
